stem: A client is starting inhaled fluticasone for maintenance asthma therapy. Which instruction helps reduce a common local adverse effect?

options.A: Use fluticasone only when acute wheezing begins because inhaled corticosteroids are intended to provide rapid bronchodilation during an asthma attack.
options.B: Swallow water immediately after each dose so medication remaining in the mouth is carried into the stomach and continues the anti-inflammatory effect.
options.C: Rinse the mouth with water without swallowing after each inhaled dose to help reduce the risk of oropharyngeal candidiasis.
options.D: Avoid any valved holding chamber because spacers increase oral drug deposition and therefore increase the risk of candidiasis during inhaled corticosteroid treatment.

rationale: Current fluticasone propionate inhalation-aerosol labeling directs patients to rinse the mouth with water without swallowing after inhalation to help reduce oropharyngeal candidiasis. It is maintenance therapy and is not indicated for acute bronchospasm. A misuses it as rescue therapy, B incorrectly tells the client to swallow the rinse, and D contradicts the label, which permits a valved holding chamber in appropriate patients.
educational_objective: Teach clients using inhaled fluticasone to rinse the mouth with water without swallowing after each inhaled dose to reduce oropharyngeal candidiasis risk.
source_organization: DailyMed / U.S. Food and Drug Administration labeling
source_document_title: Fluticasone Propionate Inhalation Aerosol prescribing information
source_locator: Dosage and Administration §2.1 Administration Information; Warnings and Precautions §5.1 Oropharyngeal Candidiasis; §5.2 Acute Asthma Episodes; Indications and Usage, Limitations of Use.
source_claim_supported: After inhalation, rinse the mouth with water without swallowing to reduce oropharyngeal candidiasis; fluticasone is not rescue treatment for acute bronchospasm; a valved holding chamber may be used in appropriate patients.

source_original.stem: A client is starting inhaled fluticasone for maintenance asthma therapy. Which instruction helps reduce a common local adverse effect?

options.A: Use fluticasone only when acute wheezing begins, because inhaled corticosteroids are intended to provide rapid bronchodilation during an asthma attack.
options.B: Swallow water immediately after each dose so medication remaining in the mouth is carried into the stomach and continues the anti-inflammatory effect.
options.C: Rinse the mouth with water without swallowing after each inhaled dose to help reduce the risk of oropharyngeal candidiasis from local corticosteroid exposure.
options.D: Avoid any valved holding chamber because spacers increase oral drug deposition and therefore increase the risk of candidiasis during inhaled corticosteroid treatment.

source_original.rationale: Current fluticasone HFA labeling instructs patients to rinse the mouth with water without swallowing after inhalation to reduce the risk of oropharyngeal candidiasis. Option C matches that instruction. Option A misuses a maintenance corticosteroid as a rescue bronchodilator. Option B tells the client to swallow rather than spit the rinse. Option D incorrectly discourages holding-chamber use.
source_original.source_detail: DailyMed Fluticasone Propionate HFA — Dosage and Administration §2.1 and Warnings/Precautions §5.1: rinse mouth with water without swallowing after inhalation to reduce oropharyngeal candidiasis; not indicated for acute bronchospasm.
